generator_noise_specification.note: These stochastic terms are deliberately generated and not independent estimated real sensor-error distributions. Day-to-day future schedule and physiological innovations cannot be denoised from today's measurements without changing target or introducing unavailable information.

journal_structure.note: Unique full text still has only 12 generated opening templates. This is limited language diversity, not duplicate sensor rows to delete.

recommended_experiment: Parent-prespecified comparison: unchanged RF versus FIT-only exclusion or weight 0.25 for extreme rows. Define extremes using any of four personal-baseline deltas with absolute robust z >4.5, median and MAD fitted within fitting fold only. Freeze rule before fits; keep all held-out observations untouched, retain person-disjoint folds, include forward-time checks, and report removed class/event composition after fitting. This respects derived feature identities because inputs are not independently clipped. The chief risk is suppressing intended HR/HRV anomaly examples, not repairing proven errors. Do not promote solely on reused validation or alter source CSV. A filtering win is evidence about this synthetic development setup, not proof that removed rows are erroneous.
do_not_do: Do not delete intentional injected anomalies from the anomaly detector's task.
Do not filter using target_current_physiology_event_injected or any future target.
Do not relabel outcomes using a predictor or delete rows simply because the model predicts them poorly.
Do not trim the evaluation distribution; all held-out rows, including tails and rare High examples, must remain.
Do not independently clip derived/baseline/current columns; that breaks their exact engineering relationships.
Do not smooth across people, use centered future windows, or claim unknown irreducible noise was removed.
